Contract: OCI image contract: HomeHub supplies the JSON config plus read-only source/config and writable source-state/backup/change/log bind mounts; SourceStatePath stores the source hash-cache MANIFEST.csv outside the read-only source. The one-shot container returns 0 only for a complete run and deposits Windows/POSIX recovery entry points. One BackupSet per container invocation — HomeHub runs one service/invocation per directory (ruled 2026-08-21); multi-set configs are a native-Windows convenience. HomeHub owns mount-identity preflight, scheduling, retention POLICY, and NagLight translation around that exit status; Retention: HomeHub owns the POLICY, FileBackup owns the MECHANISM. HomeHub must never delete a Snapshot_* folder directly — dedup means one snapshot's bytes can be the only physical copy other snapshots recover by hash. The container exposes `snapshots` (read-only inventory: name, date, row count, physical bytes, and bytes-reclaimed-if-pruned, which only FileBackup can compute because of dedup) and `prune` with an explicit snapshot name (`FILEBACKUP_SNAPSHOT` / `-Snapshot`, plus `FILEBACKUP_DRY_RUN` / `-WhatIf` for a dry run), implemented by the exported `Remove-BackupSnapshot` verb (`Prune-` is not an approved PowerShell verb): it re-homes still-referenced bytes into the surviving pool, proves every surviving manifest still resolves, and only then deletes the folder. A leading positional word in {backup, prune, snapshots} or FILEBACKUP_ACTION selects the action; any argument starting with '-' passes through to FileBackup.ps1 exactly as before. Pruning needs the /backup mount writable as well as /changes. Prune reports through the same table as backup and restore: 0 pruned / 1 batch incomplete but no data lost / 2 usage or precondition (nothing mutated) / 3 manifest-witness verification failed (nothing mutated) / 4 host I/O failure, retriable — precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1. NagLight translation: 0 ok; 1 warn (partial, no data lost, retry); 2 error, do not retry; 3 error, ESCALATE (a backup-integrity alarm, not a retention alarm); 4 warn + retry. There is no bash prune: reconstruct.sh stays restore-only and pruning is never required in order to restore. See README 'Run as a Linux container'. Restore outcome is reported through the exit-code table documented in README 'Restore exit codes' (0 complete; 1 content unrecoverable; 2 usage/precondition; 3 manifest-witness verification failure; 4 host/dependency failure - retriable), NARROWED 2026-08-26 by kit revision 8 and ratified with the counterparty: the 1-vs-4 split is decided by the stored BYTES, not by the manifest Compressed column, so an object carrying no 7-Zip signature that reproduces neither form is reported as content damage (1) rather than a retriable extraction failure (4) - a wrapper that retries on 4 therefore no longer loops over corruption. An object that IS archive-shaped and fails to open stays 4), identical for RECONSTRUCT.bat and reconstruct.sh; a restore origin's MANIFEST.csv is witnessed by MANIFEST.csv.meta which both restorers verify before writing anything (SR-038/SR-039/SR-040). "The configuration contract is the versioned JSON document specified by SR-042/SR-063 and published as `container/FileBackup.schema.json`: a required integer `ConfigVersion` (currently **2**; version 1 is refused as TOO OLD because its key set carried the removed `PreserveFolderTree` layout selector), a closed schema (any unrecognized key aborts the run naming that key), a JSON boolean `CompressEnabled`, optional `SourceStatePath` (default `SourcePath`) and `AllowEmptySource` (default `false`), and no `Secrets.Credential` (JSON cannot carry a PSCredential — containerized runs are `-NoMail`). CLIXML remains the unversioned legacy native-Windows form. Reaffirming the 2026-08-21 ruling: **one BackupSet per container invocation** — HomeHub runs one service/invocation per directory; a JSON config with more than one set is accepted for native-Windows use but logs a warning and is outside this contract. With `-ExitCode` (set by `container/entrypoint.sh`) the run reports 0 complete / 1 a backup set failed / 2 configuration or usage error, the same usage-precondition class as the restore table (SR-042/SR-043)." The container additionally exposes `verify` (and `verify` with FILEBACKUP_REPAIR=1) as an action word: an opt-in storage-form audit of the live backup and every snapshot that mutates nothing and reports on the same exit-code table (0 nothing to report, 1 findings, 2 precondition). A backup run whose estimated additions do not fit the backup or change volume refuses before writing anything, naming the volume, the requirement and the free space, and fails that set (status 1) rather than the invocation. Storage is content-addressed unconditionally (SR-058, WP9 2026-08-25): the `PreserveFolderTree` mirror layout was removed and a config still carrying the key is refused BY NAME with a removal diagnostic, so a stale HomeHub config fails loudly rather than being silently reinterpreted. The generated browse view (SR-062, config keys `BrowseView`/`ViewPath`) is deliberately OUTSIDE this contract for v1 and is NOT an action word of the container image: the view must be written outside both roots and on the backup volume, which a container's separate `/backup` bind mount cannot satisfy, so `BrowseView: index` is native-host functionality until a later IF-001 revision rules on a container view mount. The container's action words stay {backup, prune, snapshots, verify}.
